questions.knowledgeNote: Power rule plus constant multiple: 5x^3 integrates to (5/4)x^4; the +c records the family of antiderivatives.
questions.question: Q1(i). Find the indefinite integral: integral of 5x^3 dx.
questions.solution: Use the power rule integral of x^n dx = x^(n+1)/(n+1) + c for n = 3, then the constant multiple rule: integral 5x^3 dx = 5 * x^4/4 + c = (5/4)x^4 + c. Check by differentiating: d/dx[(5/4)x^4] = (5/4)(4x^3) = 5x^3. Boxed (5/4)x^4 + c (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q1(i); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: n + 1 = 7/2, so the reciprocal factor is 2/7 and the 7 cancels it exactly.
questions.question: Q1(ii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of 7x^(5/2) dx.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q1(ii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Negative exponent: divide by -5/2, i.e. multiply by -2/5, then by the coefficient 2.
questions.question: Q1(iii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of 2x^(-7/2) dx.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q1(iii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The coefficient 4 cancels the 1/4 from the power rule, leaving -x^(-4).
questions.question: Q1(iv). Find the indefinite integral: integral of 4x^(-5) dx.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q1(iv); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Term-by-term integration of a polynomial; one constant c for the whole sum.
questions.question: Q2(i). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (x^2 + 2) dx.
questions.solution: Integrate term by term: integral x^2 dx = x^3/3 and integral 2 dx = 2x. Sum: (1/3)x^3 + 2x + c. Check: d/dx[(1/3)x^3 + 2x] = x^2 + 2. Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q2(i); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The coefficients 3 and 2 are exactly cancelled by the power-rule denominators 3 and 2.
questions.question: Q2(ii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (3x^2 + 2x + 1) dx.
questions.solution: Integrate each term: 3 * x^3/3 = x^3, 2 * x^2/2 = x^2, integral 1 dx = x. Sum: x^3 + x^2 + x + c. Check by differentiation: 3x^2 + 2x + 1. Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q2(ii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Each exponent rises by 1 and is divided by its new value: 3/4 -> 7/4, 1/2 -> 3/2, 1/3 -> 4/3.
questions.question: Q2(iii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (x^(3/4) + x^(1/2) + 4x^(1/3)) dx.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q2(iii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: There is no product rule for integrals, so multiply the brackets out before integrating.
questions.question: Q2(iv). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (2x + 1)(3x + 2) dx.
questions.solution: Expand first: (2x + 1)(3x + 2) = 6x^2 + 4x + 3x + 2 = 6x^2 + 7x + 2. Integrate: 6x^3/3 + 7x^2/2 + 2x = 2x^3 + (7/2)x^2 + 2x + c. Check: d/dx = 6x^2 + 7x + 2. Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q2(iv); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: A negative power integrates to a smaller negative power: x^(-2) -> x^(-1)/(-1) = -1/x, so the minus signs give +1/x.
questions.question: Q2(v). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (x^2 - 1/x^2) dx.
questions.solution: Write 1/x^2 as x^(-2): integral x^2 dx - integral x^(-2) dx = x^3/3 - x^(-1)/(-1) = (1/3)x^3 + 1/x + c. Check: d/dx[(1/3)x^3 + x^(-1)] = x^2 - x^(-2). Boxed (printed key p571: (1/3)x^3 + 1/x + c).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q2(v); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Convert the surds to powers before integrating; note the minus sign survives on the second term.
questions.question: Q2(vi). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (sqrt(x) - 1/sqrt(x)) dx.
questions.solution: Rewrite with fractional indices: sqrt(x) = x^(1/2) and 1/sqrt(x) = x^(-1/2). Then integral x^(1/2) dx = (2/3)x^(3/2) and integral x^(-1/2) dx = x^(1/2)/(1/2) = 2x^(1/2). Hence (2/3)x^(3/2) - 2x^(1/2) + c. Check: d/dx = x^(1/2) - x^(-1/2). Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q2(vi); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Distribute the sqrt(x) first: x^(1/2) x^2 = x^(5/2) and x^(1/2) x = x^(3/2) under the root-free form.
questions.question: Q2(vii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sqrt(x)(x^2 - 5) dx.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q2(vii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Either expand or substitute y = x - 3; both give (1/3)x^3 - 3x^2 + 9x + c, equal to (x-3)^3/3 + c.
questions.question: Q2(viii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (x - 3)^2 dx.
questions.solution: Expand: (x - 3)^2 = x^2 - 6x + 9. Integrate: x^3/3 - 3x^2 + 9x + c. Check: d/dx = x^2 - 6x + 9 = (x - 3)^2. Boxed (printed key p571). (The substitution y = x - 3 gives the same answer in the compact form (x - 3)^3/3 + c.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q2(viii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Split the fraction before integrating: the 2/x term is the only one that produces a logarithm.
questions.question: Q2(ix). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (3x^2 - 5x + 2)/x dx.
questions.solution: Divide term by term: (3x^2 - 5x + 2)/x = 3x - 5 + 2/x. Integrate: 3x^2/2 - 5x + 2 log x + c. Check: d/dx = 3x - 5 + 2/x, which is the integrand. Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q2(ix); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Three separate standard integrals: constant -> ax, 1/x -> log x, x^(-2) -> -1/x.
questions.question: Q2(x). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (ax^2 + bx + c)/x^2 dx.
questions.solution: Divide by x^2: (ax^2 + bx + c)/x^2 = a + b/x + c x^(-2). Integrate: ax + b log x + c x^(-1)/(-1) = ax + b log x - c/x + k. Check by differentiating: a + b/x + c/x^2. Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q2(x); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Add the exponents (2 - 1/3 = 5/3 etc.), then integrate each; 3 * 3/5 = 9/5 and 5 * 3/2 = 15/2.
questions.question: Q2(xi). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (x^2 + 3x + 5) x^(-1/3) dx.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q2(xi); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Linear inner function: divide by the inner derivative 3, hence the 1/15.
questions.question: Q3(i). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (3x + 5)^4 dx.
questions.solution: Substitute y = 3x + 5, so dy = 3 dx and dx = dy/3. Then integral (3x + 5)^4 dx = (1/3) integral y^4 dy = (1/3) y^5/5 + c = (3x + 5)^5/15 + c. Check: d/dx[(3x+5)^5/15] = (5(3x+5)^4 * 3)/15 = (3x+5)^4. Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q3(i); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The inner derivative is -b, so the answer carries the factor -1/b.
questions.question: Q3(ii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (a - bx)^5 dx.
questions.solution: Put y = a - bx, dy = -b dx, so dx = -dy/b. Then integral (a - bx)^5 dx = -(1/b) integral y^5 dy = -(1/b) y^6/6 + c = -(a - bx)^6/(6b) + c. Check: d/dx[-(a-bx)^6/(6b)] = -(6(a-bx)^5(-b))/(6b) = (a-bx)^5. Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q3(ii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: n = -3/2 gives n + 1 = -1/2, so the factor is -2, and the inner derivative d divides.
questions.question: Q3(iii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (c + dx)^(-3/2) dx.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q3(iii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: With y^(1/2) the 1/2 and the 2 cancel, so the answer is just sqrt(2x+7) + c.
questions.question: Q3(iv). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx/sqrt(2x + 7).
questions.solution: Write the integrand as (2x + 7)^(-1/2). Put y = 2x + 7, dy = 2 dx: integral = (1/2) integral y^(-1/2) dy = (1/2) * 2y^(1/2) + c = sqrt(2x + 7) + c. Check: d/dx sqrt(2x+7) = 2/(2 sqrt(2x+7)) = 1/sqrt(2x+7). Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q3(iv); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Two independent integrals; the shifted inverse square integrates to minus the inverse.
questions.question: Q3(v). Find the indefinite integral: integral of [x + 1/(x + 3)^2] dx.
questions.solution: Split: integral x dx + integral (x + 3)^(-2) dx = x^2/2 + (x + 3)^(-1)/(-1) + c = (1/2)x^2 - 1/(x + 3) + c. Check: d/dx[(1/2)x^2 - (x+3)^(-1)] = x + (x+3)^(-2). Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q3(v); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The inner derivative 5 divides, so the second term is -1/(5(5x+1)).
questions.question: Q3(vi). Find the indefinite integral: integral of [4 + 1/(5x + 1)^2] dx.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q3(vi); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Improper fraction: write the numerator as (x-3) + 6 so the division is exact up to a log term.
questions.question: Q3(vii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (x + 3)/(x - 3) dx. (T.U. 2049 H)
questions.solution: Divide out: (x + 3)/(x - 3) = (x - 3 + 6)/(x - 3) = 1 + 6/(x - 3). Integrate: x + 6 log(x - 3) + c. Check: d/dx = 1 + 6/(x-3) = (x-3+6)/(x-3) = (x+3)/(x-3). Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q3(vii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The printed key fixes the reading of this stacked fraction as (3x-1)/(x-2): only then does the answer come out as 3x + 5 log(x-2).
questions.question: Q3(viii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (3x - 1)/(x - 2) dx.
questions.solution: Divide out: 3x - 1 = 3(x - 2) + 5, so the integrand is 3 + 5/(x - 2). Integrate: 3x + 5 log(x - 2) + c. Check: d/dx = 3 + 5/(x-2) = (3x - 6 + 5)/(x - 2) = (3x - 1)/(x - 2). Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q3(viii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Divide first: the quotient is x + 2 and the remainder 1 gives the log term.
questions.question: Q3(ix). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (x^2 + 3x + 3)/(x + 1) dx.
questions.solution: Polynomial division: (x^2 + 3x + 3) = (x + 1)(x + 2) + 1, so the integrand is x + 2 + 1/(x + 1). Integrate: (1/2)x^2 + 2x + log(x + 1) + c. Check by differentiating: x + 2 + 1/(x+1) = (x^2 + 3x + 3)/(x + 1). Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q3(ix); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Remainder theorem in practice: x^2 + 5 at x = -2 is 9, which is the numerator of the residual fraction.
questions.question: Q3(x). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (x^2 + 5)/(x + 2) dx. (T.U. 2056 S)
questions.solution: Divide: x^2 + 5 = (x + 2)(x - 2) + 9, so the integrand is x - 2 + 9/(x + 2). Integrate: (1/2)x^2 - 2x + 9 log(x + 2) + c. Check: x - 2 + 9/(x+2) = (x^2 - 4 + 9)/(x + 2) = (x^2 + 5)/(x + 2). Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q3(x); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Replace x by y - 1 so the whole integrand becomes a sum of powers of y.
questions.question: Q4(i). Find the indefinite integral: integral of x sqrt(x + 1) dx.
questions.solution: Put y = x + 1, so x = y - 1 and dx = dy. Then integral x sqrt(x+1) dx = integral (y - 1)y^(1/2) dy = integral (y^(3/2) - y^(1/2)) dy = (2/5)y^(5/2) - (2/3)y^(3/2) + c = (2/5)(x+1)^(5/2) - (2/3)(x+1)^(3/2) + c. Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q4(i); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Two factors of 1/a appear: one from dx and one from x = (y-b)/a, hence 1/a^2.
questions.question: Q4(ii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of x sqrt(ax + b) dx.
questions.solution: Put y = ax + b, so x = (y - b)/a, dx = dy/a. Then the integral is (1/a) integral ((y - b)/a) y^(1/2) dy = (1/a^2)[integral y^(3/2) dy - b integral y^(1/2) dy] = (1/a^2)[(2/5)y^(5/2) - (2/3)b y^(3/2)] + c, with y = ax + b. Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q4(ii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The factor 2x is exactly y - 3, which keeps the algebra clean; the 1/2 from dx halves the result.
questions.question: Q4(iii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of 2x sqrt(2x + 3) dx.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q4(iii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Same pattern as Q4(iii) with the inner derivative 5; the 1/5 from dx produces 2/25 and 4/15.
questions.question: Q4(iv). Find the indefinite integral: integral of 5x sqrt(5x + 2) dx. (HSEB 2051)
questions.solution: Put y = 5x + 2, so 5x = y - 2 and dx = dy/5. Then the integral is (1/5) integral (y - 2)y^(1/2) dy = (1/5)[(2/5)y^(5/2) - 2(2/3)y^(3/2)] = (2/25)y^(5/2) - (4/15)y^(3/2) + c, with y = 5x + 2. Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q4(iv); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The substitution turns x + 2 into (y + 4)/3, so both terms are powers of y; factor 2/9 at the end.
questions.question: Q4(v). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (x + 2) sqrt(3x + 2) dx.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q4(v); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: 2x + 3 becomes (2y + 7)/3 after y = 3x + 1; the 1/9 combines with the factors to give 2/9 outside.
questions.question: Q4(vi). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (2x + 3) sqrt(3x + 1) dx. (T.U. 2054)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q4(vi); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The 5 combines with 2/5 to give 2, which is why the outer factor simplifies from 1/16 to 1/8.
questions.question: Q4(vii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (5x + 3) sqrt(4x + 1) dx.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q4(vii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Splitting the numerator is enough: two single powers of y, no product rule needed.
questions.question: Q4(viii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (x + 2)/sqrt(x + 1) dx.
questions.solution: Put y = x + 1, so x + 2 = y + 1 and dx = dy. Then the integral is integral (y + 1)y^(-1/2) dy = integral (y^(1/2) + y^(-1/2)) dy = (2/3)y^(3/2) + 2y^(1/2) + c = (2/3)(x+1)^(3/2) + 2(x+1)^(1/2) + c. Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q4(viii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: 3 * (2/3) = 2 in the first term and 1 * 2 = 2 in the second - both coefficients come out as 2.
questions.question: Q4(ix). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (3x + 4)/sqrt(x + 1) dx.
questions.solution: Put y = x + 1, so 3x + 4 = 3y + 1 and dx = dy. Then the integral is integral (3y + 1)y^(-1/2) dy = 3(2/3)y^(3/2) + 2y^(1/2) = 2y^(3/2) + 2y^(1/2) + c = 2(x+1)^(3/2) + 2(x+1)^(1/2) + c. Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q4(ix); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: After the substitution both terms are single powers; the answer is printed with the factor 2/9 taken out.
questions.question: Q4(x). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (2x + 1)/sqrt(3x + 2) dx.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q4(x); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: For a negative power under a square root, the antiderivative raises the exponent: y^(-3/2) integrates to -2y^(-1/2), and y^(-1/2) to 2y^(1/2).
questions.question: Q4(xi). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (2x + 3)/(3x + 1)^(3/2) dx.
questions.solution: Put y = 3x + 1, so x = (y - 1)/3, 2x + 3 = (2y + 7)/3 and dx = dy/3. Then the integral is (1/9) integral (2y + 7)y^(-3/2) dy. Now integral y * y^(-3/2) dy = integral y^(-1/2) dy = 2y^(1/2) and integral y^(-3/2) dy = -2y^(-1/2). Hence (1/9)[2(2y^(1/2)) + 7(-2y^(-1/2))] = (2/9)[2y^(1/2) - 7y^(-1/2)] + c, with y = 3x + 1. Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q4(xi); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Both coefficients collapse to 2, so the bracket is simply y^(3/2) + y^(1/2) inside the factor 2/25.
questions.question: Q4(xii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (3x + 2)/sqrt(5x + 3) dx. (T.U. 2055 S)
questions.solution: Put y = 5x + 3, so x = (y - 3)/5, 3x + 2 = (3y + 1)/5 and dx = dy/5. Then the integral is (1/25) integral (3y + 1)y^(-1/2) dy = (1/25)[3(2/3)y^(3/2) + 2y^(1/2)] = (2/25)[y^(3/2) + y^(1/2)] + c, with y = 5x + 3. Boxed (printed key p571).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q4(xii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The conjugate factor turns the surd denominator into 1; the problem then collapses to two power integrals.
questions.question: Q5(i). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx/[sqrt(x + 1) - sqrt(x)].
questions.solution: Rationalise the denominator: multiply numerator and denominator by sqrt(x + 1) + sqrt(x). The denominator becomes (x + 1) - x = 1, so the integrand is exactly sqrt(x + 1) + sqrt(x). Integrate: (2/3)(x + 1)^(3/2) + (2/3)x^(3/2) + c = (2/3)[(x + 1)^(3/2) + x^(3/2)] + c. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q5(i); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The rationalising factor produces the constant 2a in the denominator, which combines with 2/3 to give 1/(3a).
questions.question: Q5(ii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx/[sqrt(x + a) - sqrt(x - a)].
questions.solution: Multiply by the conjugate sqrt(x + a) + sqrt(x - a); the denominator becomes (x + a) - (x - a) = 2a, a constant. Hence the integral is (1/(2a)) integral [sqrt(x + a) + sqrt(x - a)] dx = (1/(2a))[(2/3)(x + a)^(3/2) + (2/3)(x - a)^(3/2)] + c = (1/(3a))[(x + a)^(3/2) + (x - a)^(3/2)] + c. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q5(ii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Difference of the radicands is 4, so the conjugate leaves 1/4 in front; each surd then contributes 1/3.
questions.question: Q5(iii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx/[sqrt(2x + 1) - sqrt(2x - 3)]. (T.U. 2051 H)
questions.solution: Multiply by sqrt(2x + 1) + sqrt(2x - 3): the denominator becomes (2x + 1) - (2x - 3) = 4. So the integral is (1/4) integral [sqrt(2x + 1) + sqrt(2x - 3)] dx. Now integral sqrt(2x + 1) dx = (1/3)(2x + 1)^(3/2) and integral sqrt(2x - 3) dx = (1/3)(2x - 3)^(3/2) (each inner derivative is 2). Hence (1/4)(1/3)[(2x + 1)^(3/2) + (2x - 3)^(3/2)] + c = (1/12)[(2x + 1)^(3/2) + (2x - 3)^(3/2)] + c. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q5(iii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The general case: the constant left by rationalising is a + b, so the answer carries 2/(3(a+b)).
questions.question: Q5(iv). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx/[sqrt(x + a) - sqrt(x - b)].
questions.solution: Multiply by the conjugate sqrt(x + a) + sqrt(x - b); the denominator becomes (x + a) - (x - b) = a + b. Hence the integral is (1/(a + b)) integral [sqrt(x + a) + sqrt(x - b)] dx = (1/(a + b))[(2/3)(x + a)^(3/2) + (2/3)(x - b)^(3/2)] + c = (2/(3(a + b)))[(x + a)^(3/2) + (x - b)^(3/2)] + c. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q5(iv); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The inner derivative 5 divides the answer: -(1/5)cos 5x.
questions.question: Q6(i). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sin 5x dx.
questions.solution: Use integral sin(ax) dx = -(1/a)cos(ax) + c with a = 5: integral sin 5x dx = -(1/5)cos 5x + c. Check: d/dx[-(1/5)cos 5x] = (1/5)(5 sin 5x) = sin 5x. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q6(i); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Linear argument: divide by the coefficient a, the constant b does not affect the answer.
questions.question: Q6(ii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sin(ax + b) dx.
questions.solution: Put y = ax + b, dy = a dx: integral sin(ax + b) dx = (1/a) integral sin y dy = -(1/a)cos y + c = -(1/a)cos(ax + b) + c. Check by differentiating: -(1/a)(-a sin(ax + b)) = sin(ax + b). Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q6(ii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The coefficient of x here is a^2, so the dividing factor is a^2 (not a).
questions.question: Q6(iii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of cos(a^2 x + b) dx.
questions.solution: Put y = a^2 x + b, dy = a^2 dx: integral cos y dy/a^2 = (1/a^2) sin(a^2 x + b) + c. Check: d/dx[(1/a^2)sin(a^2 x + b)] = (1/a^2)a^2 cos(a^2 x + b) = cos(a^2 x + b). Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q6(iii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The antiderivative of sec^2 is tan; the inner coefficient 2 divides.
questions.question: Q6(iv). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sec^2(2x + 3) dx.
questions.solution: Since d/dx[tan u] = sec^2 u * u', integral sec^2(2x + 3) dx = (1/2)tan(2x + 3) + c. Check: d/dx[(1/2)tan(2x+3)] = (1/2)sec^2(2x+3)*2 = sec^2(2x+3). Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q6(iv); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Never integrate a square directly: linearise with the half-angle identity first.
questions.question: Q6(v). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sin^2(ax) dx.
questions.solution: Use the double-angle identity sin^2 t = (1 - cos 2t)/2 with t = ax: integral sin^2(ax) dx = (1/2) integral [1 - cos(2ax)] dx = (1/2)[x - sin(2ax)/(2a)] + c. Check by differentiating: (1/2)[1 - cos(2ax)] = sin^2(ax). Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q6(v); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The companion half-angle identity gives the plus sign: (1/2)[x + sin(2bx)/(2b)].
questions.question: Q6(vi). Find the indefinite integral: integral of cos^2(bx) dx.
questions.solution: cos^2 t = (1 + cos 2t)/2 with t = bx: integral cos^2(bx) dx = (1/2) integral [1 + cos(2bx)] dx = (1/2)[x + sin(2bx)/(2b)] + c. Check: (1/2)[1 + cos 2bx] = cos^2(bx). Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q6(vi); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: tan^2 has no antiderivative of its own form; writing it as sec^2 - 1 makes both terms standard.
questions.question: Q6(vii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of tan^2(ax) dx.
questions.solution: Use tan^2 t = sec^2 t - 1 with t = ax: integral tan^2(ax) dx = integral [sec^2(ax) - 1] dx = (1/a)tan(ax) - x + c. Check: d/dx[(1/a)tan ax - x] = sec^2(ax) - 1 = tan^2(ax). Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q6(vii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Reduce sin^4 to a sum of cosines of multiple angles; the standard result is (1/32)(12x - 8 sin 2x + sin 4x).
questions.question: Q6(viii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sin^4 x dx.
questions.solution: Use sin^2 x = (1 - cos 2x)/2 twice: sin^4 x = [(1 - cos 2x)/2]^2 = (1/4)[1 - 2cos 2x + cos^2 2x] = (1/4)[1 - 2cos 2x + (1 + cos 4x)/2] = (3/8) - (1/2)cos 2x + (1/8)cos 4x. Integrate: (3/8)x - (1/4)sin 2x + (1/32)sin 4x + c = (1/32)[12x - 8 sin 2x + sin 4x] + c. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q6(viii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Each multiple-angle term is divided by its own inner coefficient (2n and 4n), giving the 1/(32n) factor.
questions.question: Q6(ix). Find the indefinite integral: integral of cos^4(nx) dx.
questions.solution: The same reduction with t = nx: cos^4 t = (3/8) + (1/2)cos 2t + (1/8)cos 4t. Hence integral cos^4(nx) dx = (3/8)x + (1/2)sin(2nx)/(2n) + (1/8)sin(4nx)/(4n) + c = (3/8)x + sin(2nx)/(4n) + sin(4nx)/(32n) + c = (1/(32n))[12nx + 8 sin 2nx + sin 4nx] + c. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q6(ix); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Split into sec^2 + csc^2 and integrate each to tan x and -cot x.
questions.question: Q6(x). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx/(cos^2 x sin^2 x).
questions.solution: Write the integrand as sec^2 x csc^2 x. Since sec^2 x csc^2 x = sec^2 x (1 + cot^2 x) = sec^2 x + sec^2 x cot^2 x, and sec^2 x cot^2 x = cos^2 x/(cos^2 x sin^2 x) = csc^2 x, the integrand is sec^2 x + csc^2 x. Integrate: tan x - cot x + c. Check: d/dx[tan x - cot x] = sec^2 x + csc^2 x. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q6(x); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Rewrite everything in sin and cos, expand, and use the half-angle identity once for sin^2 x.
questions.question: Q6(xi). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx/(sec^2 x tan^2 x).
questions.solution: 1/(sec^2 x tan^2 x) = cos^2 x * cos^2 x/sin^2 x = cos^4 x/sin^2 x = (1 - sin^2 x)^2/sin^2 x = 1/sin^2 x - 2 + sin^2 x. Integrate: integral csc^2 x dx = -cot x, integral 2 dx = 2x, integral sin^2 x dx = x/2 - sin 2x/4. So the result is -cot x - 2x + x/2 - sin 2x/4 + c = -cot x - (3/2)x - (1/4)sin 2x + c. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q6(xi); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Half-angle identity under the root; dividing by the inner coefficient n/2 doubles the constant.
questions.question: Q7(i). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sqrt(1 + cos nx) dx.
questions.solution: 1 + cos nx = 2cos^2(nx/2), so sqrt(1 + cos nx) = sqrt(2) cos(nx/2). Then integral sqrt(2)cos(nx/2) dx = sqrt(2) * sin(nx/2)/(n/2) + c = (2 sqrt 2/n) sin(nx/2) + c. Check: d/dx[(2 sqrt2/n) sin(nx/2)] = (2 sqrt2/n)(n/2)cos(nx/2) = sqrt2 cos(nx/2). Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q7(i); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The minus version of the half-angle identity gives a sine under the root and hence a cosine in the answer.
questions.question: Q7(ii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sqrt(1 - cos px) dx.
questions.solution: 1 - cos px = 2sin^2(px/2), so sqrt(1 - cos px) = sqrt(2) sin(px/2). Then integral sqrt(2) sin(px/2) dx = sqrt(2) * (-cos(px/2)/(p/2)) + c = -(2 sqrt 2/p) cos(px/2) + c. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q7(ii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Perfect square behind the root: sin^2 + cos^2 + 2 sincos = (sin + cos)^2.
questions.question: Q7(iii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sqrt(1 + sin 2ax) dx.
questions.solution: 1 + sin 2ax = sin^2(ax) + cos^2(ax) + 2 sin(ax)cos(ax) = (sin ax + cos ax)^2, so on the positive branch sqrt(1 + sin 2ax) = sin ax + cos ax. Integrate: -(1/a)cos ax + (1/a)sin ax + c = (1/a)(sin ax - cos ax) + c. Check by differentiating: (1/a)(a cos ax + a sin ax) = sin ax + cos ax. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q7(iii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Convert the denominator into a single cosine, which turns the integral into sec^2(mx/2)/2.
questions.question: Q7(iv). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx/(1 + cos mx).
questions.solution: 1 + cos mx = 2cos^2(mx/2), so the integrand is (1/2)sec^2(mx/2). Integrate: (1/2) * tan(mx/2)/(m/2) + c = (1/m)tan(mx/2) + c. Check: d/dx[(1/m)tan(mx/2)] = (1/m)sec^2(mx/2)(m/2) = (1/2)sec^2(mx/2) = 1/(1 + cos mx). Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q7(iv); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The companion case: 1 - cos gives a csc^2 and hence a minus cotangent.
questions.question: Q7(v). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx/(1 - cos nx).
questions.solution: 1 - cos nx = 2sin^2(nx/2), so the integrand is (1/2)csc^2(nx/2). Integrate: (1/2) * (-cot(nx/2))/(n/2) + c = -(1/n)cot(nx/2) + c. Check: d/dx[-(1/n)cot(nx/2)] = -(1/n)(-csc^2(nx/2))(n/2) = (1/2)csc^2(nx/2). Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q7(v); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Rationalising with the conjugate turns the denominator into cos^2 ax, giving two standard integrals.
questions.question: Q7(vi). Find the indefinite integral: integral of dx/(1 - sin ax).
questions.solution: Multiply numerator and denominator by (1 + sin ax): the denominator becomes 1 - sin^2 ax = cos^2 ax, so the integrand is (1 + sin ax)/cos^2 ax = sec^2 ax + tan ax sec ax. Integrate: (1/a)tan ax + (1/a)sec ax + c = (1/a)(tan ax + sec ax) + c. Check by differentiating: sec^2 ax + sec ax tan ax, which is the rewritten integrand. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q7(vi); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Convert the product into a sum of sines before integrating; no product rule for integrals exists.
questions.question: Q8(i). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sin 6x cos 2x dx.
questions.solution: Use 2 sin A cos B = sin(A + B) + sin(A - B) with A = 6x, B = 2x: sin 6x cos 2x = (1/2)[sin 8x + sin 4x]. Integrate: (1/2)[-cos 8x/8 - cos 4x/4] + c = -cos 8x/16 - cos 4x/8 + c. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q8(i); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Product-to-sum for sine times sine carries the 1/2 and a minus on the higher-frequency term.
questions.question: Q8(ii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sin 7x sin 5x dx.
questions.solution: Use 2 sin A sin B = cos(A - B) - cos(A + B): sin 7x sin 5x = (1/2)[cos 2x - cos 12x]. Integrate: (1/2)[sin 2x/2 - sin 12x/12] + c = sin 2x/4 - sin 12x/24 + c. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q8(ii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: sin(A - B) with A < B is negative, which is why the second term gains a plus after integration.
questions.question: Q8(iii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of sin 6x cos 8x dx.
questions.solution: 2 sin 6x cos 8x = sin 14x + sin(-2x) = sin 14x - sin 2x, so the integrand is (1/2)[sin 14x - sin 2x]. Integrate: (1/2)[-cos 14x/14 + cos 2x/2] + c = -cos 14x/28 + cos 2x/4 + c. Boxed (printed key p572, printed as cos 2x/4 - cos 14x/28 + c).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q8(iii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The general product-to-sum form; each multiple-angle sine is divided by its own coefficient.
questions.question: Q8(iv). Find the indefinite integral: integral of cos px cos qx dx.
questions.solution: Use 2 cos A cos B = cos(A + B) + cos(A - B): cos px cos qx = (1/2)[cos(p + q)x + cos(p - q)x]. Integrate: (1/2)[sin(p + q)x/(p + q) + sin(p - q)x/(p - q)] + c. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q8(iv); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: integral e^(kx) dx = e^(kx)/k: the negative exponent gives the minus sign in front.
questions.question: Q9(i). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (e^(px) + e^(-qx)) dx.
questions.solution: Integrate each exponential separately: integral e^(px) dx = e^(px)/p and integral e^(-qx) dx = e^(-qx)/(-q) = -e^(-qx)/q. Sum: e^(px)/p - e^(-qx)/q + c. Check by differentiating: e^(px) + e^(-qx). Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q9(i); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: The cross term is 2e^(px)e^(-px) = 2, a constant, which integrates to 2x.
questions.question: Q9(ii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (e^(px) + e^(-px))^2 dx.
questions.solution: Expand the square: e^(2px) + 2 + e^(-2px). Integrate: e^(2px)/(2p) + 2x + e^(-2px)/(-2p) + c = e^(2px)/(2p) + 2x - e^(-2px)/(2p) + c. Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q9(ii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Splitting the fraction reduces the problem to three standard exponentials.
questions.question: Q9(iii). Find the indefinite integral: integral of (e^(2x) + e^x + 1)/e^x dx.
questions.solution: Divide term by term: e^(2x)/e^x = e^x, e^x/e^x = 1, 1/e^x = e^(-x), so the integrand is e^x + 1 + e^(-x). Integrate: e^x + x - e^(-x) + c. Check by differentiating: e^x + 1 + e^(-x). Boxed (printed key p572).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.1 Q9(iii); book p569-571 = PDF p596-598; key book p571-572 = PDF p598-599

questions.knowledgeNote: Multiplying powers adds exponents: x + 2x = 3x.
questions.question: Q9(iv). Find the indefinite integral: integral of e^x(e^(2x) + 1) dx.
questions.solution: Expand: e^x e^(2x) + e^x = e^(3x) + e^x. Integrate: e^(3x)/3 + e^x + c. Check: d/dx = e^(3x) + e^x. Boxed (printed key p572).
